name: A House Divided and Remade
description: Cotton, conscience and conflict: how slavery split the United States, how the Civil War was fought and won, and how freedom was won and then contested.

checkpoints.name: Cotton and chains
checkpoints.note: The cotton gin makes slave-grown cotton hugely profitable and ties the South to the Atlantic slave trade. Sojourner Truth, Frederick Douglass and Harriet Tubman fight slavery, and Uncle Tom's Cabin turns it into a national cause.

checkpoints.name: The road to war
checkpoints.note: The new Republican Party opposes the spread of slavery, John Brown's raid terrifies the South, and the election of Abraham Lincoln leads Southern states to leave the Union.

checkpoints.name: The war
checkpoints.note: The Confederate States fight the Union under Robert E. Lee and Ulysses S. Grant. Gettysburg turns the war, the Emancipation Proclamation and Gettysburg Address give it a new purpose, and the Thirteenth Amendment ends slavery.

checkpoints.name: Reconstruction
checkpoints.note: Reconstruction tries to give freed people citizenship through the Fourteenth Amendment, but it ends when federal troops leave the South.

checkpoints.name: The unfinished work
checkpoints.note: Segregation holds for nearly a century, until Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King Jr. and a mass movement win the Civil Rights Act and the Voting Rights Act.
